title: Muscle oxygen saturation (SmO2): An upstream metabolic link connecting peripheral muscle metabolism to central neurobiological adaptations
title_zh: 肌肉氧饱和度（SmO2）：连接外周肌肉代谢与中枢神经生物学适应的上游代谢通路
abstract: Physical activity (PA) and neuropsychology have been associated, although the peripheral mechanisms that connect skeletal muscle activity to central nervous system remain unclear. Various muscle derived signaling molecules, including myokines and metabolites, are released due to PA. Lactate is one of the signaling molecules released via muscle during PA and it may serve as an intermediatory metabolite which links peripheral muscle metabolism to central neurobiological adaptations. Along with it, PA also induces alterations in muscle oxygen saturation (SmO2), reflecting changes in local metabolic stress and mitochondrial demand. SmO2 plays a vital role in exercise physiology but still how it impacts neuropsychology has not received attention. Reductions in muscle oxygenation due to PA has been associated with elevated lactate production, while lactate itself acts as an energy substrate, signaling molecules, and epigenetic modulators within the brain, promoting BDNF expression and neuroplastic processes. In this review, we propose that SmO2 can act as an upstream physiological signal within a SmO2-lactate-brain axis, translating peripheral metabolic stress into positive neuropsychological outcomes. Establishment of SmO2 as a non-invasive biomarker of neuropsychology could act as a novel model to understand the interactions between PA and brain. This can help to optimize interventions based on PA aiming to enhance cognition, emotional resilience and neurological health.
abstract_zh: 物理活动（PA）与神经心理学已被关联，但连接骨骼肌活动与中枢神经系统的外周机制仍不清楚。多种肌源性信号分子，包括肌细胞因子和代谢物，因PA而释放。乳酸是肌肉在PA期间释放的信号分子之一，可能作为中间代谢物，将外周肌肉代谢与中枢神经生物学适应联系起来。与此同时，PA还会导致肌肉氧饱和度（SmO2）的改变，反映局部代谢应激和线粒体需求的变化。SmO2在运动生理学中起重要作用，但其对神经心理学的影响尚未受到关注。PA导致的肌肉氧合下降与乳酸产生升高相关，而乳酸本身在大脑中既是能量底物，又是信号分子和表观遗传调节因子，促进BDNF表达和神经可塑性过程。在本综述中，我们提出SmO2可作为SmO2-乳酸-大脑轴中的上游生理信号，将外周代谢应激转化为积极的神经心理学结果。将SmO2确立为神经心理学的非侵入性生物标志物，可作为理解PA与大脑相互作用的新模型。这有助于优化基于PA的干预，以提升认知、情绪韧性和神经健康。
